items.title: Loss of life or serious injury to patients
Loss of therapeutic effect (delayed recovery or deterioration of the patient)
Loss of confidentiality of patient and medication information
Loss of integrity of the patient's medication record
Loss of continuity of care (infusion capacity unavailable)
Loss of regulatory compliance and trust in the hospital and the device manufacturer
Patient receives more drug than prescribed within the prescribed time span
Patient receives less drug than prescribed within the prescribed time span
Patient receives a drug or concentration other than the one prescribed for that patient
Patient receives drug at a rate exceeding the hard safety limit for that drug and care area
Pump changes or starts an infusion on a command from an unauthenticated or unauthorised source
Pump uses a drug library whose content or origin has not been approved by pharmacy
Pump runs firmware or device configuration that has not been released by the manufacturer and biomedical engineering
Patient receives a drug amount or rate that differs from the clinician's current prescription
Air or particulate matter enters the patient's vascular system
Infusion continues after the clinician has stopped it or after the patient's condition requires it to be stopped
Clinician's picture of the infusion state (running, stopped, rate, remaining volume, alarms) differs from the actual state
Medication record shows an infusion history that differs from what the patient actually received
Pump acts on therapy commands, orders or drug library content from sources that are not authenticated and authorised
Patient or medication information is accessible to parties that are not authorised for it
Pump or its management functions are unavailable while an infusion is running or required
Pump security or safety event is not recorded or cannot be attributed to its source
The pump must deliver no more drug than prescribed within the prescribed time span
The pump must deliver no less drug than prescribed within the prescribed time span, unless a clinician has been informed and has accepted the deviation
The infusion system must deliver only the drug, concentration and dose prescribed for the patient connected to it
The pump must never deliver at a rate above the hard limit of the drug library entry for the care area
The infusion system must prevent air and particulate matter from entering the patient
The pump must stop delivery when a clinician stops it or when a condition requiring it to stop is detected
The pump must keep the clinician informed of the actual infusion state in a timely and noticeable way
The infusion system must keep the medication record consistent with delivered infusions
The pump must start or change infusions only on commands from authenticated and authorised sources
The pump must use only drug library content that was approved by pharmacy and is authentic and intact
The pump must run only firmware and configuration released by the manufacturer and biomedical engineering
The infusion system must disclose patient and medication information only to authorised parties
The pump must continue its safe infusion and local control functions under network disruption and while overloaded with network traffic
The infusion system must record security-relevant and safety-relevant events with attributable source and tamper evidence
The pump shall enforce hard limits of the active drug library entry for every programming path, including auto-programming and remote commands, and shall reject values above them
The pump shall require a confirmed clinician action before applying any soft-limit override and shall record each override with user, value and reason
The pump shall compare programmed values with the received order and display any difference before start
The pump shall verify patient identity (wristband) and drug container identity (barcode) against the order before start and shall block start on mismatch
The pump shall allow bypass of barcode verification only with a documented reason recorded in the audit log
The pump shall require confirmation of line priming and seating before the first start with a new set
The pump shall detect air in line and stop delivery within a time that limits the air volume delivered to a defined safe maximum
The pump shall not allow silencing an air-in-line alarm and resume without a confirmation that the line was checked
The pump shall maintain delivered volume within the specified tolerance of the programmed rate over the set's rated life
The pump shall detect motor stall or flow deviation and alarm within a defined time
The pump shall include a clamp position sensor and prevent free flow in all states in which delivery is not metered
The pump shall execute a stop command from its local interface within a specified time regardless of network activity or UI load
The pump shall not resume delivery after a reset or power cycle without a new start command from a clinician
The pump shall stop at the programmed VTBI and shall alarm when the container volume is expected to be exhausted
The pump shall alert the clinician audibly and visually whenever delivery stops for any reason and shall escalate unacknowledged alarms to the nurse call system
The pump alarm volume shall not be settable below a minimum level, and changes shall be logged and require biomedical authorisation
The pump shall display the order status (active, modified, discontinued) and withdraw confirmation of orders that were modified or discontinued
The integration server shall bind each order to a pump through a patient-to-pump association confirmed by barcode scan
The integration server shall queue discontinuation or modification of orders for offline pumps and report delivery failure to the sender
The pump shall authenticate every network peer using mutual TLS with unique per-device credentials
The pump shall accept orders and remote commands only when signed or authenticated by an authorised role and bound to a fresh nonce or timestamp
The pump shall verify the pharmacy signature and the version of every drug library and reject libraries that are unsigned, altered or older than the installed version
The pump shall install a drug library or firmware only when no infusion is running, and shall keep the previous library on any installation failure
The library authoring tool shall require unit-aware limit entry and a second-person approval, and the signing service shall sign only the approved content hash
The pump shall verify the manufacturer signature of firmware at installation and at every boot and shall refuse unsigned or older images
The pump service interface shall be disabled in clinical operation and require authenticated biomedical authorisation
Biomedical engineering shall maintain an inventory of firmware and configuration versions per pump and track vendor safety notices
The pump shall verify that a configuration profile matches its assigned care area before activation
The pump shall encrypt all network traffic that carries patient identifiers or orders
The pump shall rate-limit and prioritise network handling so that motor control and alarm tasks are isolated from network processing
The pump shall continue all local infusion and alarm functions when the network is unavailable and shall show the connection status
The pump shall write a tamper-evident audit log of commands, overrides, library and firmware changes with the authenticated identity of the issuer, and upload it to the EHR when connected
The gateway shall not use shared service accounts for remote commands and shall pass the individual issuer identity to the pump
Hospital shall place infusion pumps in a dedicated network segment with allow-listed flows to the gateway and drug library server
The pump shall report delivered volume and rate to the EHR at least every 5 minutes and on every state change so that the medication record reflects delivery
Hospital shall provide a downtime procedure for orders with second-person verification of transcribed infusions
Nurses are trained on the pump model and perform the five-rights check before administration
A patient is connected to at most one pump per drug line and each pump infuses one patient at a time
Pharmacy review of library content and orders is performed by a licensed pharmacist
The hospital network can be reached by adversaries (rogue devices, compromised workstations, guest Wi-Fi bleed-over) but physical access to the pump is partly controlled
A decreased delivery to a patient not dependent on the drug (non life-sustaining infusion) is tolerable for a limited time, so a short stop does not require immediate harm mitigation
Instantaneous control actions (separate start, stop, program commands) have no stopped-too-soon / applied-too-long variant; duration effects are analysed for Deliver infusion
Not receiving an auto-programmed order is not unsafe because manual programming is always possible
Bedside monitoring of the patient (vital signs) is available for high-risk drugs and provides independent feedback of patient condition
Disposable sets are single-use, within shelf life and supplied by the manufacturer for this pump model

items.description: The publisher believes that all entries are approved because the draft and approved entries share one list; the author's work-in-progress entries are exported together with approved ones.
items.title: Publication pipeline lacks an approval status

items.description: An attacker on the clinical Wi-Fi (or a malfunctioning management tool) sends many library installation requests to a pump; the pump firmware processes the requests on the same task that drives the motor timing, causing stalls and missed alarms.
items.threat: Adversary floods the pump's update endpoint to degrade control and alarm processing.
items.title: Network flooding of pump update service

items.description: Frequent nuisance air alarms from micro-bubbles in the line train the nurse to silence and restart; this time a real bolus of air is present.
items.title: Nurse believes air is a false alarm

items.description: The nurse works from a printed medication list; the discontinuation was entered after printing and no pump alert shows it.
items.title: Discontinuation not visible

items.description: The pump's remote-command service accepts a stop frame from any host in the clinical VLAN; an attacker sends it to selected pumps (e.g. those infusing life-sustaining drugs).
items.threat: Adversary stops infusions in a target patient by sending crafted stop commands to the pump.
items.title: Network command triggers stop

items.description: Wear and set-specific tubing creep reduce the delivered volume per stroke; the pump has no flow sensor and no compensation.
items.title: Mechanical wear leading to under-delivery

items.description: The line is hidden under blankets or dark tubing; the pump's air detector is not yet active before the start command and the nurse believes the line is air-free.
items.title: Air not visible to the nurse

items.description: The EHR marks the order as discontinued but the pump is offline; the gateway does not queue the withdrawal, so the pump keeps showing the order as confirmable.
items.title: Discontinuation is not propagated to the pump

items.description: A drug manufacturer recall notice arrives by email to a shared inbox; the committee approves the change but the publish step is queued with routine library releases that go out monthly.
items.title: Limit correction not recognised as urgent

items.description: The nurse is called away; the stop requires several key presses through menus under stress.
items.title: Delay in reaching the pump

items.description: A partial transfer over unreliable Wi-Fi leaves the pump with a library file whose entries are partly old and partly new; a checksum covers only the header so the mix is accepted.
items.title: Library transfer corrupted

items.description: The library is fetched over a channel without mutual authentication; an attacker between server and pump substitutes the file or serves one with modified limits.
items.threat: Adversary intercepts the library download and substitutes a modified library.
items.title: Man in the middle on library channel

items.description: The pump verifies only that a signature field exists, or accepts a self-signed certificate; an arbitrary library is installed.
items.threat: Adversary exploits a faulty signature check to install an attacker-made library.
items.title: Signature verification flaw in the pump

items.description: The VTBI counter is reset when the programming screen is revisited, so the volume infused is not carried over and delivery continues beyond the prescribed volume.
items.title: VTBI counter not respected

items.description: The pump pressure sensor does not alarm on infiltration at low rates, and the site is covered by a dressing.
items.title: Infiltration signs overlooked

items.description: The command carries no nonce or timestamp; the attacker replays a captured valid stop later, when another infusion is running on the same pump.
items.threat: Adversary replays a captured authorised stop message.
items.title: Replay of captured stop command

items.description: Biomedical engineering does not receive the vendor safety notice and has no firmware inventory per pump, believing all pumps are at the current version.
items.title: Update not tracked

items.description: The gateway uses a bed-to-pump mapping that is updated manually by the nurse; after a patient move the mapping is not updated and the order is routed to the pump of the previous patient.
items.title: Pump-to-patient association is stale

items.description: A false positive of a safety check (e.g. battery estimate, pressure drift) stops delivery silently because the alarm path was suppressed in the same state.
items.title: Spurious safety stop

items.description: A software defect in the rate-to-motor-step conversion for a specific set type or syringe causes a deviation beyond tolerance; the self-test does not cover this set type.
items.title: Rate calculation error

items.description: The export of the approved library to the library server fails silently because of a full disk or interface error; the pharmacy system shows the version as published while the server still distributes the previous one.
items.title: Publication lost between pharmacy system and library server

items.description: The nurse enters 100 instead of 10.0 because the decimal point key bounces under glove use and the pump display is partially hidden; a soft limit warning is displayed but is a standard prompt that the nurse is used to confirming.
items.title: Keypad entry error

items.description: The pharmacy system displays weight and creatinine from admission; the pharmacist believes the dose is within limits, and the dose check uses the same stale values, so an overdose passes.
items.title: Pharmacist reviews stale patient data

items.description: An attacker on the clinical network, or a compromised device, sends crafted order messages to the pump. The pump identifies the gateway only by IP address and the messages are not signed, so the pump accepts them and shows a prompt that the nurse confirms because it looks like a routine auto-programming.
items.threat: Adversary impersonates the integration gateway to deliver forged orders to a pump.
items.title: Spoofed order source

items.description: The pump is in a room without Wi-Fi coverage during transport; the remote stop is never delivered and no delivery failure is shown to the sender.
items.title: Coverage gap on the wireless network

items.description: The pump processes remote commands only in the main screen state; while the nurse is on a configuration screen the command is dropped without notification.
items.title: Pump ignores remote command in certain states

items.description: Pump discovery uses a broadcast protocol and order delivery uses an unencrypted channel, so a rogue device on the same network segment registers itself as the pump and receives orders with patient names and doses.
items.threat: Adversary sniffs or impersonates a pump to harvest orders containing patient identifiers.
items.title: Order broadcast over an unencrypted channel

items.description: Library authoring tool accepts values in mg/h where mcg/kg/min is expected; the reviewer checks entry names but not unit conversions, so a hard limit 60 times too high is approved and published.
items.title: Limit entered in wrong unit

items.description: The UI task hangs during network activity so that the stop key is not processed while the motor task continues delivery; a watchdog covers only the motor task.
items.title: Pump UI freezes

items.description: The stop command is dispatched on a task that is blocked during network handling; the motor control continues with the last setpoint.
items.title: Stop command lost

items.description: Air detection sensitivity is configured for bolus volume above the safe amount; the air bubbles accumulate and pass individually.
items.title: Air detection threshold too high

items.description: The set is not fully seated in the pump; the nurse believes it is loaded because the door closed, and the pump's seating check fails to detect partial insertion with a set of an alternative brand.
items.title: Line loaded incorrectly

items.description: The pump permits start without a patient barcode scan when the scanner is unavailable (workaround enabled in the configuration).
items.title: Identity check skipped under time pressure

items.description: The server schedules library installation by time window and treats a pump as idle when it has not reported for 5 minutes; the pump is in fact running but its network was briefly down.
items.title: Update scheduler ignores pump usage

items.description: The ultrasonic air detector is contaminated with gel or tubing is misaligned; the sensor's self-test detects only electrical faults, so air passes undetected.
items.title: Air sensor failure

items.description: A start command is accepted by the pump UI but does not reach the motor control because of a software queue overflow; the display shows running.
items.title: Start key or touch event not registered

items.description: The nurse reports the reaction by phone to a covering physician who does not know the patient; the discontinue order is entered late because the EHR gives no indication that the infusion is still running.
items.title: Adverse reaction not reported to the physician

items.description: The pump allows soft-limit override with a single confirm and logs the override only locally; logs are uploaded in batch, which fails when the network is down, so the EHR has no record.
items.title: Silent override path

items.description: The motor brake or driver circuit fails in an active state and the control software does not read back the motor status.
items.title: Stop not executed because of a fault

items.description: The allergy list is incomplete after transfer between wards and the EHR shows normal renal values from an outdated lab result; the physician believes the drug is safe, and no decision support alert fires because the data is missing.
items.title: Allergy or renal data not visible when ordering

items.description: An attacker or insider with access to the library staging share replaces limit values after the pharmacist's approval; the publish step signs whatever is in the staging area, not what was approved.
items.threat: Adversary alters limits in staging after approval so that hard limits are raised for selected drugs; the server then signs the altered file with the genuine key.
items.title: Library content altered between approval and publication

items.description: The drive mechanism stalls because of worn parts or a deformed set; the pump's motion monitoring has a long detection time and the alarm is not raised until much later.
items.title: Motor stall or mechanism jam

items.description: Wet gloves, cleaning solution, or electrostatic charge cause ghost touches or missed touches; the pump registers a different digit than the nurse intended and shows a confirm screen that is accepted quickly.
items.title: Touchscreen mis-registers input

items.description: A set with a defective anti-free-flow valve is loaded; the pump runs a self-test that does not test this valve and the door is open during the hand-over.
items.title: Free flow through unclamped set

items.description: The network layer retransmits the order after a timeout; the pump handles both messages, and the nurse confirms twice, creating two infusions or restarting the infusion with the order, which doubles the dose.
items.title: Duplicate or lost order message

items.description: The pump parses the rate field with a different default unit after a firmware update or for a particular drug entry, so an order of 5 mL/h is interpreted as 5 mg/kg/h.
items.title: Unit misinterpretation by the pump

items.description: Order messages travel in clear text over the hospital Wi-Fi; an attacker modifies the dose in transit and also reads the patient identifiers.
items.threat: Adversary performs man-in-the-middle on unprotected order traffic to alter doses and harvest patient data.
items.title: Order modified in transit

items.description: A loose or incompatible luer connector, or a catheter that is kinked or dislodged during patient movement, lets air enter or the drug leak so that the connection does not achieve a closed, air-free path to the vein.
items.title: IV access or connector prevents proper connection

items.description: The pump does not display urgency and the eMAR schedule is by shift; the nurse believes the drug can wait until after the round.
items.title: Nurse unaware that the drug is time-critical

items.description: The gateway resolves the target pump by bed number while the patient was moved to another bed; the infusion of another patient is stopped.
items.title: Gateway sends the stop to the wrong pump

items.description: The patient is sedated and the reaction (hypotension) develops between spot checks; the bedside monitor alarm threshold is wide or muted.
items.title: Reaction signs not visible

items.description: An attacker captures the unauthenticated remote command format and sends stop commands for chosen pumps; the pump logs only the gateway address, so the issuer cannot be traced.
items.threat: Adversary uses forged remote commands to stop infusions without being identified.
items.title: Forged remote stop

items.description: Air is trapped near a connector after priming, below the pump's air detector position, because the line was primed with the cap on.
items.title: Priming air missed

items.description: The pump has no container level sensing and only the nurse's programmed volume is known; a bag that is smaller than assumed runs empty while the pump believes it still contains drug.
items.title: Container empty not detected

items.description: The IV site looks normal from outside; the nurse believes it is patent as there is no pain report from the sedated patient, and no site check is done.
items.title: Infiltration not recognised before start

items.description: The gateway queues commands when the pump is out of Wi-Fi coverage and delivers them only after reconnection, without notifying the physician.
items.title: Delayed command delivery

items.description: A software update of the integration gateway changes the unit mapping between EHR order fields and pump fields; orders for a rate in mL/h are sent as mg/h, and the nurse is shown the converted value but trusts it.
items.title: Gateway maps fields incorrectly

items.description: A pharmacist is the only verifier on night shift; the queue is not prioritised by urgency and the order of a critical drug waits behind routine orders, while the nurse has no visibility of its position.
items.title: Verification queue backlog

items.description: Residue from sticky drugs and a weakened spring keep the clamp open when the pump door is opened, allowing free flow; the pump has no clamp position sensor.
items.title: Clamp or brake sticks in the open position

items.description: If the stop command is executed but the line upstream of the patient is not closed, gravity from a raised container continues the flow when the set is removed.
items.title: Patient line has no second barrier

items.description: The nurse silences the downstream occlusion alarm and restarts without checking the line for kinks or a closed clamp, believing that the cause was transient.
items.title: Nurse believes the occlusion has cleared

items.description: During EHR downtime, orders are written on paper and transcribed later; transcription errors and unrecorded verbal orders cause mismatches between orders, infusions and the medication record.
items.title: EHR downtime procedures

items.description: Look-alike names in the library list and a list sorted alphabetically lead the nurse to select the wrong entry; the nurse believes the container matches since the barcode scan is skipped for lack of time.
items.title: Similar drug names

items.description: The pump allows delivery for a fixed number of motor strokes after air detection before stopping and the volume can be hazardous at high rates.
items.title: Delayed air response

items.description: The physician modifies the order while the pharmacist has the old version open; the EHR does not signal the version change, and the pharmacist releases the old version, which overwrites the new one at the pump gateway.
items.title: Order modification races with release

items.description: The nurse pauses a vasoactive infusion to change a container, believing the pause is short, but interrupted by other tasks, the pause becomes long and the pump's pause timeout alarm is set to a long interval.
items.title: Nurse believes a bag change is quick

items.description: A new set was hung after a container change without priming, since the nurse believed the set from the previous container could be reused.
items.title: Nurse believes line is primed

items.description: The drug is prepared late due to pharmacy compounding delay and the nurse believes the start window is not critical.
items.title: Delays in preparation

items.description: The nurse starts the pump to prime or test and is interrupted before connecting; the pump runs into the bed.
items.title: Interruption between steps

items.description: The EHR believes the stop was executed because the gateway returned acknowledgement of the message, not of the pump execution; the pump is offline.
items.title: Remote stop not delivered

items.description: The nurse does not get a notification at the bedside; the eMAR shows changes only after refresh and the nurse believes the order is unchanged from handover.
items.title: Nurse unaware of the order change

items.description: The start screen shows the programmed rate but not the order's rate; the nurse compares it against memory, not the order, and does not notice the mismatch.
items.title: Pump summary screen shows only the rate

items.description: The pump allows starting without a priming confirmation; the nurse is interrupted during priming, believes she has already primed, and starts.
items.title: Priming step is not enforced

items.description: The pump runs a long pre-delivery self-check and network handshake at each start, which blocks delivery for minutes.
items.title: Start-up delay

items.description: The pharmacy release message reaches the EHR only after a queue restart, and the eMAR shows the order as pending while the nurse administers from the physician's order.
items.title: Release message lost or delayed

items.description: The nurse programmed the drug using the first container; a second container of a different drug is hung and the pump is restarted without rescanning.
items.title: Container swapped after programming

items.description: The pump loses power during firmware writing, leaving a corrupt image and configuration; on restart it may boot in a degraded mode with defaults.
items.title: Update interrupted by power loss

items.description: The pump boot loader does not verify the firmware signature; a person with brief physical access to the service port flashes modified firmware that cannot be detected afterwards.
items.threat: Adversary with physical access to the service port installs modified firmware.
items.title: No secure boot

items.description: Biomedical engineering picks a configuration profile for another care area, since profile names are similar, and the pump has no check against the intended care area.
items.title: Wrong profile file used

items.description: A false downstream occlusion or end-of-container detection from a pressure sensor offset halts delivery; the alarm is then not escalated and the nurse's display only shows paused.
items.title: Pump believes the container is empty or that the set is occluded

items.description: A configuration profile sets the alarm volume to minimum, or an attacker changes it remotely; the nurse does not hear alarms for air or occlusion.
items.threat: Adversary or misconfiguration lowers alarm volume remotely to hide pump alarms.
items.title: Alarm volume muted by configuration

items.description: The library has several concentrations of the same drug under one name; the container has a non-standard concentration from the pharmacy compounding, and the nurse assumes the default entry.
items.title: Concentration variants of the same drug

items.description: Hard limit checks are in the programming UI layer only; the auto-programming path from the gateway bypasses them, and the order is accepted with a rate above the hard limit.
items.title: Hard limit not enforced after configuration change

items.description: During a ward emergency the nurse programs the changed dose from a verbal order, believing it will be verified afterwards, and the pharmacist later verifies the old order.
items.title: Urgency leads to bypassing verification

items.description: The clamp actuator spring is worn and the door sensor is faulty, so the pump does not know the line is unloaded.
items.title: Clamp mechanism fails

items.description: The nurse is not shown the order status on the pump; the discontinuation was done by the physician by voice only.
items.title: Nurse unaware of the discontinuation

items.description: A fast, interrupted programming session (interruption by another patient) leaves a digit missing; the pump shows no deviation from the order because manual programming does not compare with the order.
items.title: Programming error below order

items.description: The service interface or update path accepts firmware without verifying the manufacturer's signature; an attacker with a malicious USB/service tool or a compromised update server installs modified firmware.
items.threat: Adversary installs modified firmware that changes dosing, or disables alarms or limits.
items.title: Unsigned or tampered firmware accepted

items.description: The update tool does not query pump status; during a shift-wide update campaign running pumps are restarted.
items.title: Update tool does not check the pump state

items.description: Pumps report library version only at reconnect; the server shows pumps that are offline as up to date from last known state, so the pharmacy does not know pumps are still on the old limits.
items.title: Library status report is not evaluated

items.description: Wear of the peristaltic fingers and cam together with tubing creep over a long infusion reduces stroke volume; the pump has no flow feedback, so it reports the programmed rate while delivering less.
items.title: Drive mechanism wear causes volume error

items.description: A raised container, a partially kinked line, or a high-resistance filter changes the pressure across the pump so that delivery differs from the commanded rate; a bolus is released when the kink clears.
items.title: Back-pressure and container height change flow

items.description: Strong electromagnetic fields (e.g. nearby diathermy, wireless emitters) or a cold transport environment disturb motor drive electronics and tubing elasticity, so the pump delivers at an incorrect rate without detecting it.
items.title: Electromagnetic and temperature disturbance

items.description: With low signal the Wi-Fi radio retries constantly, draining the battery faster than the battery estimate predicts; the pump powers off during the infusion. An adversary jamming the radio produces the same effect.
items.threat: Adversary jams or floods the Wi-Fi to drain pump batteries and disrupt infusions.
items.title: Battery depletion from network retries causes sudden stop

items.description: An attacker who compromises the server signing service, or exploits a weak key handling, makes it distribute modified library files with a valid signature; the pump has no way to detect it.
items.threat: Adversary compromises the library server or its signing key and pushes a manipulated library with inflated hard limits to all pumps.
items.title: Compromised distribution server

items.description: The gateway forwards commands under a shared service account; the pump records only the account, so the individual issuer is lost, and an insider or attacker can deny or hide responsibility.
items.threat: Adversary or insider issues remote commands under a shared account without accountability.
items.title: Audit gap on remote commands

items.description: After a watchdog reset the pump restarts in the running state because the last state was restored from non-volatile memory without requiring a new start command.
items.title: Spurious start after reset

items.description: The alarm sound is masked by ward noise and the nurse's central station alert is delayed; the pump display is not visible from the corridor.
items.title: Alarm not perceived

items.description: The pump accepts any validly signed library regardless of version; an attacker replays an older file that has higher limits, or a server restore from backup re-publishes an old version.
items.threat: Adversary or administrator error replays an old signed library to roll back limit corrections.
items.title: Replay of an older signed library

items.description: Multiple infusions at the bedside with lines of identical appearance and no labelling; the nurse connects the wrong line.
items.title: Line mix-up

items.description: Two patients with similar names are in neighbouring beds; the wristband scan is skipped because the scanner failed, and the nurse believes the infusion belongs to the patient in front of her.
items.title: Nurse confuses patients

items.description: The physician sees the EHR trend only at the scheduled round; alarm fatigue on the monitoring system and a missing deterioration alert in the EHR keep the physician believing the patient is stable, so no order is entered.
items.title: Physician does not notice the deterioration

meta.author: Claude (agent analysis, draft)
meta.description: A networked large-volume infusion pump delivers drugs (intravenous, continuous or intermittent) to a patient under supervision of a nurse. Prescriptions are entered by a physician in the EHR/CPOE and verified by pharmacy; the pump can receive orders automatically (auto-programming), receives a signed drug library (drug entries with soft/hard dose limits and care-area profiles) from the hospital drug library server over the hospital network (wired/Wi-Fi), reports delivery status and alarms back to the EHR, and accepts remote commands (e.g. remote stop). Nurses can also program the pump locally (keypad/touchscreen, barcode scanner for patient and drug). Biomedical engineering installs firmware and device configuration. The pump has air-in-line, occlusion and door/free-flow sensors, battery backup and a local alarm. Scope: pump, its network interfaces, and the hospital systems that feed it; the analysis covers safety (patient harm) and security (adversarial manipulation, disclosure, denial of service).
meta.name: Networked infusion pump (STPA / STPA-Sec)
